Petitioner: Chikka Revamma,
 W/o Ranganath,
 Aged about 37 years,
 R/at Lakkur village & post,
 Sompura Hobli,
 Nelamangala Taluk,
 Bangalore Rural - 562 111.

-Vs- Respondents: 1.

The United India Insurance Co. Ltd.,
 Regional Office, Krishi Bhavana,
 5th floor, Hudson Circle,
 Bengaluru - 560001.(Insurer).

Policy No.1709003122P103746423  From 01.08.2022 to 31.07.2023  Lorry bearing No.KA-01-AF-9685  (By Sri B.M. Raghavendra,
 Advocate)

2. M/s Core Logistics Company,
 No.07, R.C. Complex, 206-261,
 S.G. Mutt Road, Chamarajpet,
 Bengaluru - 560 018.

(Absent)
 SCCH-1 2 MVC No.326/2023

JUDGMENT Petitioner asserting to be an injured suffered in a RTA filed petition under Section 166 of M.V.Act claiming compensation from the respondents who are the owner and insurer of the Lorry bearing No.KA-01-AF-9685 asserting that on 01.01.2023 at about 8.30 a.m. when walking on Dabaspet- Tumkur NH-48 service road, near SRS bike showroom, driver of Lorry bearing No.KA-01-AF-9685,
drove the same negligently, dashed the same to the petitioner, thereby caused accident, caused Chikka Revamma vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 5 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8134142/
1 injuries to the petitioner.
2. Petitioner took treatment at Government Hospital Dabaspete and Hemavathi Hospital, Tumkur,
as on the date of accident petitioner being aged about 37 years, used to earn Rs.25,000/p.m. by working as Maid.
3.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Regarding accident Nelamangala Traffic Police, registered crime No.4/2023 against the driver of the Lorry bearing No.KA-01-AF-9685.

4. In response to the notice, respondent No.1- Insurance Company appeared through his Advocate,
filed written statement, denying the allegation regarding reason, mode of accident, age, occupation,
income, nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.
5. In spite of service of notice, respondent No.2 - owner of the lorry has remained absent.

6. On the basis of the pleadings on 29.02.2024, this Authority has framed the following issues :
1. Whether the Petitioner proves that on 01.01.2023 at about 8.30 a.m. opposite SRS Bike showroom, Dabaspet - Tumkur NH-48 Service road, Bengaluru, she met with an accident and sustained injuries, was due to actionable negligence act on the part of the driver of the Cement Bulkar Lorry bearing registration No.KA-01-AF-9685 as alleged?
2.
Whether the Petitioner is entitled to compensation ?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order ?
7. On 29.02.2024, 17.08.2024 petitioner deposed as PW1 and produced 12 documents at Ex.P.1 to P.12.

On 16.10.2024, 04.12.2024 petitioner produced the evidence of Dr. Naveen Kumar H.R. as PW2 and get produced 2 documents at Ex.P.13 and P.14.
8.
I heard the arguments submitted on behalf of petitioner and perused the records.

9. On the basis of the record, my findings on the above issues and additional issue are as under:
Issue No.1 ...
In the affirmative Issue No.2 ...

Petitioner is entitle to receive Rs.24,30,961/-
with interest at 6% p.a. from 17.08.2024 on Rs.23,80,961/- as compensation from the respondents.
Issue No.3 ...

As per final order for the following:-
Chikka Revamma vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 5 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8134142/
2 REASONS 10. Issue No.1 :- In the evidence petitioner stated that on 01.01.2023 at about 8.30 a.m. when walking on the side of Dabaspet- Tumkur NH-48 service road, near SRS bike showroom, driver of Lorry bearing No.KA-01-AF- 9685, drove the same negligently, dashed the same to her, thereby caused accident, caused injuries to her.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 11. In the written statement respondents No.1 denied the allegation regarding reason and mode of the accident.
12. In the cross-examination petitioner/PW.1 denied the suggestion that in Dabaspet on Tumkur- Dabaspet service road 2 heavy vehicles can pass simultaneously.
Petitioner stated that when she was walking on the mud road, lorry dashed to her.
Petitioner denied the suggestion that when she was crossing the road met with the accident.

Petitioner stated that the lorry came from her back side,
except lorry no vehicles are running on the road during accident.
Petitioner denied the suggestion that as per sketch the width of the road where the accident taken place was measuring 40 feet,
therefore there was no circumstances or occasion to dash lorry to her back.
13. In the evidence PW.2- Dr. Naveen Kumar H.R. stated nothing regarding reason and mode of the accident.

14. Ex.P.1 is the copy of the FIR with complaint pertaining to crime No.4/2023 registered by Nelamangala police against driver of Lorry bearing No.KA-01-AF-9685 for having committed offence punishable under Section 279,337 of IPC, on the basis of the complaint presented by Manjunath L.K. S/o Late Kamisiddaiah.
Ex.P.2 is the copy of spot mahazar.
Ex.P3 is the copy of the motor vehicle accident report.

Ex.P4 is the copy of the charge sheet filed by Nelamangala traffic police in crime No.4/2023 against Nagaraju G. S/o Late Ganthi Deevar driver of Lorry bearing No.KA-01-AF-9685 for having committed offence punishable under Section 279, 338 of IPC.

Ex.P.5 is the copy of wound certificate issued by Hemavathi Hospital, Tumkur in which reason for the injuries suffered by the petitioner is noted as "on 01.01.2023 at around 8.45 a.m. alleged RTA near Dobaspete".
In the discharge summary marked at Ex.P.6 history is noted as RTA at around 8.45 a.m. on 01.01.2023 near Dabaspete, hit and run by lorry.
15. In this case respondents have not produced any type of evidence to disbelieve the evidence placed by the petitioner regarding reason, mode and consequence of accident.

Hence, I have concluded that on 01.01.2023 at about 8.30 a.m. when petitioner was walking on the side of Dabaspet- Tumkur NH-48 service road, near SRS bike showroom, Nagaraju G. S/o Late Ganthi Deevar - driver of Lorry bearing No.KA-01-AF-9685, drove the same negligently, dashed the same to the petitioner, thereby caused accident, caused injuries to the petitioner.
Hence, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative.

16. Issue No.2: In the evidence petitioner stated that in the accident she has suffered left lower limb circumferential degloving injury from left froin to left ankle, took treatment at Government Hospital, Dabaspete, then took treatment at Hemavathi hospital, Tumkur.

Petitioner stated that in Chikka Revamma vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 5 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8134142/
3 Hemavathi Hospital underwent wound debridement, split skin grafting of left lower limb.

entities.text: Chikka Revamma vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 5 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Petitioner further stated in Hemavathi Hospital taken treatment as inpatient from 01.01.2023 to 12.01.2023 and from 30.01.2023 to 06.02.2023 by spending Rs.7,00,000/- towards treatment, medicine,
conveyance and nourishment charges.

Petitioner stated that as on the date of accident use to earn Rs.25,000/- by working as Maid.
17.
In the written statement, respondent No.1 denied the allegation regarding nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.
18. In the cross-examination, petitioner stated that in the accident she has suffered injuries only to left leg.
Petitioner stated that she took treatment as an inpatient for period of 2  months at Hemavathi Hospital, Tumkur.
Petitioner admitted that in the accident she never suffered fracture.
Petitioner denied the suggestion about non- spending of Rs.7,00,000/- for treatment and non-earning of Rs.25,000/- per month by working as a maid.

19. In the evidence affidavit PW2 Dr.Naveen Kumar H.R. stated that on 10.10.2024 when clinically examined the petitioner noticed that petitioner suffered permanent physical disability at 30.27% to whole body.

20. In the evidence PW2 produced outpatient record and x-ray at Ex.P.13 and P.14.
21.
In the cross-examination PW2 stated that he neither treated the petitioner nor verified inpatient treatment record.
PW.2 stated that while assessing the disability verified discharge summary of Hemavathi Hospital, Tumkur.

22. Wound certificate , discharge summaries, photos, medical bills, prescriptions, X-rays and other documents shows that in the accident petitioner suffered degloving injury of left thigh and gluteal region, degloving injury to left lower limb and abrasion over right knee, took treatment at Hemavathi hospital, Tumkur as an inpatient from 01.01.2023 to 12.01.2023 and from 30.01.2023 to 06.02.2023 underwent wound debridement, skin grafting by spending Rs.6,02,961/-.

In the copy of aadhar card marked at Ex.P.7 date of birth of petitioner is noted as 07.05.1985.
23.
In the file there are no documents regarding quantum of income of the petitioner.
The deposition shows that on 17.08.2024 petitioner came to Court Hall with the help of a walker and deposed by sitting.
24. In the file there are no evidence to disbelieve the contents of medical records regarding nature of the injuries suffered, the length, place, nature of treatment taken by the petitioner.

Hence, I have inferred that in view of the injuries suffered in the accident, in spite of better treatment, petitioner suffered permanent functional disability at 35% and calculated loss of future income in the following terms:
Age of the petitioner as on the date of 37 years accident - Chikka Revamma vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 5 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8134142/
4

entities.text: Chikka Revamma vs United India Ins Co Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Notional monthly income of the petitioner Rs.16,000/- 35% permanent functional disability Rs.5,600/- Loss of future income 5,600x12x15 Rs.10,08,000/-
25.

Hence, I award Rs.10,08,000/- towards loss of future income, Rs.2,00,000/- towards Pain and Sufferings, Rs.6,02,961/- towards treatment charges, Rs.1,00,000/- towards attendant ,
conveyance, nourishment charges, Rs.3,20,000/- (16,000x20) towards loss of income during treatment period, Rs.1,50,000/- towards loss of amenities and future unhappiness, Rs.50,000/-
towards future medical expenses.

26. Since 01.01.2023 to August -2024 for the period of 20 months compensation is awarded under the head loss of income during treatment period, I came to the conclusion that the petitioner is entitle for Rs.24,30,961/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. on Rs.23,80,961/- from 17.08.2024 from the respondents as compensation (Rs. 50,000/- awarded under the head of future medical expenses does not carry interest).
27. In the written statement the respondent No.1 admitted the subsistence of the policy with respect to lorry bearing No.KA-01-AF-9685 as on the date of incident.
In the file there are no evidence to show that as on the date of incident , respondent No.2 owner of lorry bearing No.KA- 01-AF-9685 has violated any terms of the policy.

Hence, I came to the conclusion that respondents being the owner and insurer of the lorry bearing No.KA-01-AF-9685 are liable to pay compensation and an award is to be passed directing the respondents to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Hence, I answer issue No.2 accordingly and pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act is hereby partly allowed.

The respondents shall either jointly or severally pay Rs.24,30,961/- (Rupees Twenty four lakhs, thirty thousand, nine hundred sixty one only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from 17.08.2024 on Rs.23,80,961/- to petitioner towards compensation (Rs.50,000/- awarded towards future medical expenses does not carry interest).
The respondent No.1, being the Insurer of the lorry bearing No.KA-01-AF-9685 shall deposit the compensation amount with interest within 4 months from today.
After deposit of the compensation amount, 50% of the compensation amount and interest may be released to the petitioner by crediting the same to her bank account directly.

Surplus compensation amount and interest shall be deposited in the name of petitioner in any bank for a period of 5 years without permitting her to create any encumbrances, however reserving liberty to withdraw periodical interest once in 3 months.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/- .

Draw an Award accordingly.
